confirmed_facts.excerpt: Open-Source Project "GPU Unlock" Bypasses NVIDIA's Software-Level Restrictions on GeForce GPUs, Unlocking Professional-Grade Compute Capabilities A new trick has been unlocked to bypass NVIDIA's software-level restrictions on consumer GeForce graphics cards.

confirmed_facts.text: This has been achieved with a new open-source project called "GPU Unlock", which allows the GPUs to access higher half-precision floating-point compute performance, which typically is reserved for the professional workstation GPUs.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: This has been achieved with a new open-source project called "GPU Unlock", which allows the GPUs to access higher half-precision floating-point compute performance, which typically is reserved for the professional workstation GPUs.

confirmed_facts.text: "GPU Unlock" dynamically patches the NVIDIA driver module within the Linux kernel and intercepts requests for the GPU's physical PCIe Device ID before replacing the returned identifier with that of a compatible professional GPU.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: "GPU Unlock" dynamically patches the NVIDIA driver module within the Linux kernel and intercepts requests for the GPU's physical PCIe Device ID before replacing the returned identifier with that of a compatible professional GPU.

confirmed_facts.text: This basically tricks the driver into recognizing a consumer GeForce GPU as a professional NVIDIA card, bypassing the restrictions and unlocking additional compute capabilities.
confirmed_facts.excerpt: This basically tricks the driver into recognizing a consumer GeForce GPU as a professional NVIDIA card, bypassing the restrictions and unlocking additional compute capabilities.
